gemini.rationale: The customer-facing products (Mobile Devices and Home segments) transferred, but the shared corporate operational substrate they historically relied on (IT systems, financial support, legal) did not transfer whole, creating a structural mismatch at T5 (gap_45 = 1). This gap was mitigated at closing via Transition Services Agreements. The employees and management running the separated business transferred alongside it, aligning the organization with the transferred operations (gap_56 = 0).

grok.rationale: gap_45=0 because the slice states the spin-off distributed a going product operation (Mobile Devices and Home portfolio) together with the business that produced it; product and its segment operations crossed as one package into the new HoldCo. gap_56=0 because the same closing structure moved the management and ~21,000 employees that ran those businesses with them (Jha continuity; Employee Matters Agreement), so processes that transferred were aligned with their organization; shared corporate substrate that did not cross was not a transferred process stripped of its people but was instead left behind and bridged by TSAs and related separation agreements.

openai.rationale: The customer-facing Mobile Devices and Home portfolio transferred as a going product operation, but historically shared cash management, IT, audit, financial-transaction, legal, and administrative processes did not cross intact, establishing gap_45. Transition Services Agreements contractually bridged those functions for generally up to 12 months, so the documented gap was mitigated at closing. For gap_56, approximately 21,000 employees, including a portion of historically shared corporate employees, and the pre-separation management running the business moved with it; the slice therefore documents coherent organizational alignment with the transferred operations rather than a process-without-people mismatch.
